title: Open Values Decision Contracts v0.2
description: For each product or service category on Conscious Consuming, the setup of its decision page: the one-line summary of what to compare, up to three dials a reader can move, whether a budget answer can be shown, and which computed answers to show. pipeline/build_decisions.js writes it to content/decisions.json, and the dataset build copies each contract into its category file for the app to read.

format.description: Always "open-values-decision-contracts". Tells a reader which Open Values format this is.

version.description: The version of the decision contracts format this file follows. Must start with 0.2.0.

published.description: The date this set of contracts was published, as YYYY-MM-DD.

status.description: Whether the founder has approved the contracts (founder-approved) or not yet (founder-signoff-pending).

consumer.description: Notes naming the part of the site that reads each part of a contract.

contracts.description: One contract per category, each saying how that category's decision page works.

reads.description: A note naming the part of the site that shows the one-line reads, and the review round that approved them.

axes.description: A note naming the part of the site that shows the dials, and the review round that approved them.

budget.description: A note naming the part of the site that uses the budget settings, and the review round that approved them.

archetypes.description: A note naming the part of the site that shows the computed answers, and the review round that approved them.

category.description: The id of the category this contract is for, such as "plant-based-milk". It matches a category dataset in app/data/.

consumer.description: Notes for this one category that replace the file-wide consumer notes, when a category needs them.

reads.description: The one-line summary of what to compare in this category, the criteria it is based on, and who signed it off.

axes.description: The dials a reader can move on the decision page, one to three of them. Each dial shifts how much some criteria count.

budget.description: Whether the category has enough cost data for a budget answer, and which criterion holds it.

archetypes.description: Which computed answers the page shows: "best-for-most" (top result with the reader's rules and dials), "strictest-match" (the option whose weakest score on the read criteria is highest), and "budget-honest" (a cost-first rank over only the options with cost data). The last one appears only when budget data is available.

text.description: The sentence a reader sees, at most 140 characters, such as "Compare plant-based milk by environmental impact, processing, nutrition, and cost."

basis.description: The criteria the sentence names, two to five of them, each with the words used for it.

signature.description: Who approved the sentence, when, and whether it was a pilot or part of an approved batch.

receipt.description: Added by the dataset build: how many entries the category holds and, for each criterion in the read, how far scores spread, so a reader can see the criteria really separate the options.

criterion.description: The criterion key in the category dataset, such as "nutrition_grade".

readsAs.description: The words the sentence uses for that criterion, such as "nutrition".

by.description: Who approved the read, such as "Conscious Consuming".

on.description: The date of approval, as YYYY-MM-DD.

status.description: Whether the read was approved one by one as a pilot (pilot) or as part of a generated batch (approved-batch).

dataset.description: The id of the category dataset the figures were taken from.

entryCount.description: How many entries the category dataset holds.

criteria.description: For each criterion in the read that has at least two different scores, how many entries have a score and how far the scores spread.

readsAs.description: The words the read uses for that criterion.

known.description: How many entries have a score on this criterion.

minimum.description: The lowest score on this criterion, from 0 to 100.

maximum.description: The highest score on this criterion, from 0 to 100.

spread.description: The highest score minus the lowest. Always above 0.

id.description: A short name for the dial, such as "processing" or "cost-or-values".

kind.description: How the dial works: "criterion" turns one criterion up or down; "tradeoff" moves weight between two criteria; "cost-values" moves weight between the cost criterion (listed first) and the value criteria after it.

label.description: The name shown on the dial, such as "Price or overall fit".

question.description: The question shown with the dial, at most 80 characters, such as "Lower observed price or a stronger overall fit?"

criteria.description: The criterion keys the dial changes. For a cost-values dial the first is the cost criterion; for a tradeoff dial there are exactly two.

poles.description: The labels at the two ends of the dial: the first at 0, the second at 100.

default.description: Where the dial starts, from 0 to 100. 50 is the middle, where neither end is favoured.

available.description: True when at least 5 entries have a cost score and those scores differ, so a budget answer can be shown.

mode.description: Where the cost data comes from: "observed-price-rank" (prices seen in open food data), "assessed-fees-rank" (assessed fees), "assessed-affordability-rank" (assessed price or affordability), or "none" when there is not enough.

criterion.description: The criterion key that holds cost, such as "economical" or "fees".

minimumKnown.description: How many entries need a cost score before a budget answer may be shown. Currently 5.

knownEntries.description: Added by the dataset build: how many entries have a cost score. 0 when no budget answer is available.

coverage.description: Added by the dataset build: the share of entries with a cost score, from 0 to 1, rounded to four places.
